messages.subject: Error in new(...)
parts:
Dear all,

I am facing some error messages that aren't fully reproducible, but when they occur in a session once, even the simplest models are producing that error (see example below). I have updated R, RStudio, and Rtools to the newest versions (and even deleted the previous versions), and don't really know what to do next. Did anyone ever face the same issues?

Best,

Marius

#### Reproducible example (once the error occurred)

library(nimble)
code <- nimbleCode({
  y ~ dnorm(0,1)
})
model <- nimbleModel(code)

#### Error message
Error in new("code_MID_5_modelClass_UID_31_UID_32", ...) :
  unused arguments (inputList = list(list(numeric(0), numeric(0)), new("modelDefClass", .xData = <environment>), list(numeric(0))), name = character(0))

This is mysterious. Is there an .RData file (i.e. you might have selected "yes" to the "save workspace image?" query when closing R) in the working directory where you are starting R? I am wondering if something being loaded from that is clashing with the internals (dynamically-generated class definitions) that nimble does. It is just a guess.
Perry

I have updated R, RStudio, and Rtools to the newest versions (and even deleted the previous versions), and don't really know what to do next. Did anyone ever face the same issues?

Best,

Marius

library(nimble)
code <- nimbleCode({
  y ~ dnorm(0,1)
})
model <- nimbleModel(code)

messages.subject: Re: Error in new(...)
parts:
Hi Perry,

I have identified a workaround, resolving a conflict with the tidyverse packages that used tfor data manipulation.Here's the solution I used:

a) Finish all data manipulation & save as csv
b) clear the Global environment  via  rm(list=ls())
c) read in only the csv again
d)  run nimble. 

Despite this solution, I am still surprised as I made sure to adhere to good practices in working with tidyverse (such as converting tibbles back to data.frames and ensuring data was ungrouped, etc.) Again, the same code worked for me two weeks ago without any problems.

Here are the requested steps:

1)
> ls(all=TRUE)
[1] ".Random.seed"
Warning message:
R graphics engine version 16 is not supported by this version of RStudio. The Plots tab will be disabled until a newer version of RStudio is installed.

2) Sorry, I realise that I was not clear enough here. This small chunk of code would trigger it only if I use some data manipulation via dplyr beforehand; in a clean R-Session the code is executed without error. However, once the R Session got into that error, even this bit of code will result in that error.

3) nimbleModel (e,g., name = "mymodel") is the same

Best,

Marius

Perry de Valpine schrieb am Mittwoch, 18. Oktober 2023 um 15:18:58 UTC+2:
If you type 
ls(all = TRUE)
 in a fresh R session, what do you see?

Is the small bit of code you sent really all it takes to trigger this error?

What happens if you use the name argument to nimbleModel (e,g., name = "mymodel")?

Perry

On Wed, Oct 18, 2023 at 6:07 AM Marius G <mariusg...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Perry,

thanks for your prompt answer. I have never saved.RData file and checked, there is also none in my project. The error occurs in plain R, Rmd, and quarto. Even if I copy the code to a new R Session, the same error occurs, depending on the model that I am running the error message looks like this:

####
Defining model
Building model

  unused arguments (inputList = list(list(numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), 2, c(3, 3), c(3, 7), c(274, 4), c(274, 6), c(274, 4), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), c(274, 4), c(274, 4)), new("modelDefClass", .xData = <environment>), list(numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), numeric(0), 2, c(3, 3), c(3, 7), c(274, 4), c(274, 6), c(274, 4), numeric(0))), name = character(0))

I can identify some of the arguments on the input list based on their dimensions. However, the same code was not giving an error before. 

Cheers,

Marius

Perry de Valpine schrieb am Mittwoch, 18. Oktober 2023 um 14:48:48 UTC+2:
Dear Marius,
This is mysterious. Is there an .RData file (i.e. you might have selected "yes" to the "save workspace image?" query when closing R) in the working directory where you are starting R? I am wondering if something being loaded from that is clashing with the internals (dynamically-generated class definitions) that nimble does. It is just a guess.
Perry
